acceptance.criterion_verbatim: AC1 -- the registry holds family OPAL_REPORT_PDF and the repository put of that family succeeds (tests -k opal_report_pdf_family, >= 1 passed)
acceptance.denominator: 1 passed of 1 selected (75 deselected); the file's 76 tests all pass

acceptance.criterion_verbatim: AC2 -- the producer retains the PDF through put and returns its artifact_ref (tests -k retains_pdf_artifact, >= 1 passed)
AC3 -- a document larger than the checkpoint limit is persisted and its checkpoint stays within the limit (tests -k opal_document_over_checkpoint_limit, >= 1 passed)
AC4 -- the Opal checkpoint carries an artifact ref and a sha256 and not the document (tests -k opal_checkpoint_is_a_reference, >= 1 passed)
AC5 -- a v1 document persists byte-equal to what the unchanged publisher persisted (tests -k v1_document_persists_byte_equal, >= 1 passed)
AC6 -- the whole publisher test file passes (tests, all, no failure)

mutant.description: Negative arms run inside the tests: a put of a family the policy does not register is refused by the fake put (naming builder); a checkpoint reference with a wrong digest, a wrong family or a changed ref is refused and publishes nothing; an inline-size document would exceed CHECKPOINT_BYTES (asserted before the spill). No source mutation was run.
mutant.expected: each raises a refusal and persists nothing
mutant.observed: the tests pass, so every negative arm raised

determinism.method: each criterion run once under timeout 120; the whole generate and research test directories (576 passed, 30 skipped) and reports retention and generate_installed tests (31 passed) were also run once
determinism.observed: all pass; the v1 byte-equal digest test passes against the unchanged vendor branch

declared_exclusions.item: Any vendor call, AWS call, S3 or DynamoDB write, deploy; the caller wiring of artifacts into produce and of the retained ref into the checkpoint (resident_worker, cell d-6); the live registry deploy and its effect on retention rows stored under the old policy digest
